answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a jade, before it can post or attest. A single forge checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 216 aliases thus costs 99 bonds held for 18 days each, plus the anchor attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so someone cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
